title: Grateful Dead Live at Reed's Ranch on 1969-07-03
lineage: Cassette Master -> Dat (48k) > Dat (Sony R500) -> VXPocket v2 -> Samplitude Professional v10.1 -> FLAC (1 Disc Audio / 1 Disc FLAC)

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of the July 3 1969 Reed’s Ranch show shines on a monster “He Was A Friend Of Mine” solo, though the recording is occasionally gritty and the early set uneven.
ai_review.review: The performance delivers classic late‑'60s Dead magic – a soaring “He Was A Friend Of Mine,” jazzy “Morning Dew,” country‑flavored “Green Green Grass of Home” with pedal steel, and a sweet “High Time.”  The soundboard source is generally clear, letting Jerry’s guitar tone stand out, but listeners note some distortion, clipping (the MAMU intro) and a ragged start to the set.  Overall the show is praised for its historic vibe despite a few tuning hiccups and mixed audio quality.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers (≈10/14) give high marks for the music, especially “He Was A Friend Of Mine,” while a minority criticize sound quality and performance roughness; weighted average of show (≈4.0) and recording (≈3.2) yields ~3.8.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear board sound with crisp guitar, but occasional distortion, clipping on the opening MAMU and a ragged early segment; overall listenable.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend Of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: Short (~45 min) early‑'69 set with a country‑flavored opening, building into tighter jams; the vibe is historic and relaxed despite an uneven beginning.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work receives high praise, especially his solo on “He Was A Friend Of Mine.”
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil had to retune his guitar early in the show and later jokes about coffee, indicating tuning issues.
